acceptance_criteria: Project-key authentication carries project_credentials.id into ProjectScope and never substitutes project_id or the raw key.
ActorIdentityProvider and ResolveAuditActor provide fail-closed actor resolution without extending SimplePrinciple.
User principles resolve to actor type user with the user ID; project principles resolve to actor type project with the credential ID.
Organization and service principles without stable durable identities do not implement a successful actor identity and resolve as unavailable.
ScopedAuthentication adds optional actorType and actorId fields without changing existing field numbers or behavior.
ScopeAuthorize cache keys are versioned and use an HMAC-SHA256 token fingerprint rather than the raw credential.
ScopeAuthorize cache writes use a bounded five-minute TTL, so pre-change entries are ignored and new entries cannot remain indefinitely.
Existing user, organization, project, and service authentication behavior remains compatible.
non_goals: Creating organization_credentials or service identity registries.
Public resource createdActor or updatedActor fields.
SDK releases or UI actor rendering.

principles.kiss: Add one companion actor contract, propagate the existing credential primary key, and version only the affected scope-auth cache.
principles.yagni: Defer persistence, dual write, organization/service provisioning, public APIs, SDK releases, and UI work.
principles.single_source_of_truth: project_credentials.id is the sole project actor identifier; project_id remains authorization scope only.
principles.contracts: Add optional actorType field 5 and actorId field 6, preserving every existing protobuf field number and authentication response behavior.
principles.fail_safe: Authenticated actor-aware callers without a durable identity return an explicit resolver error; no scope or compatibility user is guessed.
principles.security: Use HMAC-SHA256 with the configured internal secret for cache fingerprints; never log, persist, or cache the raw project credential as actor metadata.
principles.observability: Retain existing authentication error logging without credential material; cache versioning provides deterministic rollout behavior.
principles.reversibility: Retain the versioned HMAC cache-key behavior during code rollback or delete both legacy and Phase 1A ScopeAuthorize namespaces before restoring the old client. Never reactivate unbounded legacy entries.

required_tests: actor resolver user and project success paths
actor resolver unavailable and unsupported fallbacks
all concrete principle implementations and test doubles still compile
local web user authPrinciple implements ActorIdentityProvider in a same-package test
project credential query aliases id to credential_id
web ScopeAuthorize emits project actorType and actorId
remote project authenticator rejects non-project or malformed actor identity
legacy unversioned cache entries are ignored
scope-auth cache key contains no raw token and changes with token or scope
scope-auth cache SET uses bounded TTL
protobuf descriptor preserves fields 1 through 4 and adds optional fields 5 and 6
risks: Reflection-based casting can omit actor fields unless ScopeAuthorize populates them explicitly.
Changing cache key format temporarily increases authentication service calls until versioned entries warm.
ActorIdentityProvider type assertions must cover both local authPrinciple and serialized PlainAuthPrinciple.
Generated protobuf artifacts can drift if commands regenerate unrelated files.
rollback: Revert actor/protobuf propagation before schema work while retaining the versioned HMAC cache-key behavior. If the cache code must also be reverted, first delete legacy and Phase 1A ScopeAuthorize namespaces so unbounded pre-change entries cannot reactivate.
